clue.text: Bit of food all mixed up with sour herb inside

indicators.note: inside says the herb goes within the jumbled letters
mixed up tells us the letters of the two words all and sour are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: sage is a kitchen herb

explanation.surface: A cook complains that a dish is a muddle, with a sour-tasting herb buried in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of food' sounds like a crumb, but it is the definition: a whole snack. The herb splits the jumbled seven letters into a front three and a back four.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry-wrapped tube of minced pork is a classic British snack, a small item of food.

clue.text: Help half of all the characters

indicators.note: half of means only one of the two equal parts of the word is kept, here the back four letters

parts.note: every letter from A to Z together makes up the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is told they can aid only fifty per cent of the cast in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' looks like people in a story but means letters; 'half of' keeps the back four of its eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Man to walk ahead of faint-hearted person

indicators.note: ahead of in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to step is to walk
a hen, like a chicken, stands for a coward

explanation.surface: A man strides out in front of a timid companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is a man's first name, so any man called that fits the bare definition.

clue.text: Somehow disabled in sport

definitions.meaning: a lame or injured one, so the word can mean partly disabled
a sport is a ... such as football or tennis

explanation.surface: An athlete is hampered by some unspecified injury during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' softens the first sense: a game leg is lame in some way.
explanation.definitionFit: Game means lame in an old phrase for an injured limb, and a contest such as cricket is a game.

clue.text: Go on a road as fugitive

parts.note: to go on, as a play or engine does, is to run
a way is a road or path

explanation.surface: An escaped prisoner takes to the highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive is one who has fled, which is what a runaway is.

clue.text: Hard mineral, not fine material

indicators.note: not means the letter for fine is left out of the mineral

parts.note: flint is a hard quartz stone
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A buyer is told a fabric is made of tough rock, not delicate stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Lint is a soft fabric used for dressing wounds, so it is a material.

clue.text: Injured climber, a top becoming tricky

indicators.note: injured says the letters of climber, a and top are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A mountaineer gets hurt on a summit, making the descent difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Injured' shuffles CLIMBER, A and TOP (eleven letters) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something problematic presents difficulties, the same idea as tricky.

clue.text: Critical factor put off worker — pit almost falling in

indicators.note: falling in says the shortened pit drops inside the joined first and last pieces

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for pit is dropped

parts.note: a mine is a pit

explanation.surface: A labourer is discouraged when a pit caves in on him.
explanation.walkthrough: The ant is crossword's stock worker. The shortened pit sits between the two outer pieces rather than at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A determinant is a factor that decides an outcome, so a critical factor.

clue.text: Rudest yawn's nastily given as unhelpful response

indicators.note: nastily signals the letters of rudest and yawn's are treated roughly into a new arrangement

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, giving its five letters including the S

explanation.surface: A bored listener's rude yawn serves as a dismissive reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nastily' rearranges RUDEST YAWNS; the 's here counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a curt, unsatisfying reply or a refusal, an unhelpful response.

clue.text: Ribbons and label on dog upset the French female

parts.note: a tag is a label

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them, to tail
elle is French for she

explanation.surface: A name tag on an upset dog belongs to a French woman.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta comes in long flat strips, ribbons of dough.

clue.text: Unnecessary seats in line to be shifted

indicators.note: to be shifted says the letters of seats, in and line are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Extra chairs in a row are surplus and must be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be shifted' rearranges SEATS IN LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inessential is not required, hence unnecessary.

clue.text: Way to see English being knocked out in defeat

indicators.note: being knocked out means the letter for English is removed from the word for way

parts.note: a route is a way

explanation.surface: A sports fan reflects on watching England's team eliminated in a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing, disorderly defeat.

clue.text: Water that's brown spreading across river

indicators.note: spreading across says the brown colour stretches around the river letter

parts.note: tan is a light brown
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Muddy brown water spreads across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, a body of water.

clue.text: One struggling to establish line in attack

indicators.note: in says the letter for line goes inside the word for attack

parts.note: to batter is to attack with blows

explanation.surface: A fighter tries to set up a front line during an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: A battler is a fighter who keeps struggling against difficulties.

clue.text: Wet season is predominant, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that sounds like the phrase for being predominant

parts.note: something that reigns is supreme or predominant

explanation.surface: A weather report says the rainy period is in full sway.
explanation.definitionFit: In tropical countries the rains are the monsoon months, the wet season.

clue.text: Seats become rotten aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means placed within the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
eggs addle when they go bad

explanation.surface: Chairs on a vessel are decaying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddle is the seat for a rider of a horse or bicycle.

clue.text: Ruin ground with introduction of parking

indicators.note: with introduction of says the parking letter is put into the word for ground

parts.note: soil is ground or earth
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Building a car park ruins the land.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil something is to damage or wreck it.

clue.text: Strong piece of material that may be disposable

definitions.meaning: an old word for heady, potent ale

definitions.text: piece of material that may be disposable
definitions.meaning: the British word for a baby's diaper, which may be cloth or a throwaway kind

explanation.surface: A sturdy bit of fabric can be thrown away after use.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a nappy, British for a diaper; many are disposable.
explanation.definitionFit: Nappy describes strong foaming ale, and a diaper is a piece of material often made to throw away.

clue.text: English mother offers Danish food

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal

explanation.surface: An English mum serves up Danish fare.
explanation.walkthrough: Edam is in fact a Dutch cheese, not Danish; the definition is best read as just 'food'.
explanation.definitionFit: This round red-waxed cheese is a food.

clue.text: Trim old man getting about

parts.note: the old man is slang for father, pa
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Dad is getting a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: To pare is to cut away the edges, to trim.

clue.text: Old buffoon opposing the first hint of change

parts.note: anti means against or opposing

indicators.note: the first hint of means only the opening letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A clownish elderly man resists any suggestion of change.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage an antic was a grotesque performer or clown, a buffoon.

clue.text: A project in which a learner appears perplexed

indicators.note: in which says the following pieces sit inside the word for project

parts.note: to toss is to throw or project
L is the learner-driver plate letter

explanation.surface: A student taking part in a school project is confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in which' puts A and L inside TOSS to make TALOSS after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means not knowing what to do, bewildered or perplexed.

clue.text: Bad act and more or less everybody could make it

definitions.text: Bad act and more or less everybody could make it

indicators.note: bad means the letters of act are spoilt into another order

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for approximately
all means everybody

explanation.surface: A dreadful performance draws jeers from almost the whole audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges ACT to CAT; C is circa, about. As a whole, the clue describes the jeer an awful act earns.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill whistle or jeer of disapproval is what nearly everyone in a crowd might make at a poor show.

clue.text: Helps foolish person — is crossing street

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: crossing says the word is goes across, around, the street abbreviation

explanation.surface: A clumsy fool walks across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help someone, so a matching verb form.

clue.text: Brilliant hit — hooked?

parts.note: to lam is to beat or hit
something hooked is bent

explanation.surface: A boxer's punch is praised as a great hook.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent means softly glowing or brilliantly flickering, as of light or wit.

clue.text: Romantic couple despite marriage fraying at the edges

indicators.note: fraying at the edges says the outer letters of the phrase wear away, leaving a run from inside it

explanation.surface: Two lovers stay together though their marriage is coming apart.
explanation.walkthrough: With the ends worn off, the run inside despITE Marriage remains.
explanation.definitionFit: In tabloid slang a pair who are dating are called this, a romantic couple.

clue.text: Suitable encounter from what we hear

indicators.note: from what we hear says the entry is spelt differently from a word with the same sound

parts.note: to meet someone is to encounter them

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a meeting was fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition relies on an archaic spelling of meet, 'fitting', found in the old prayer-book phrase 'meet and right'; Chambers does not list this spelling for that sense, so the clue is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: In older English the word was a variant of meet in its sense of fitting or proper, hence suitable.

clue.text: Slight rest

definitions.meaning: slight here means thin or slender
to rest against a wall is to prop oneself on it

explanation.definitionFit: Lean means thin, slender of build, and to recline against a support is to rest on it.

clue.text: Insect that is loud by meadow

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
lea is a poetic word for meadow

explanation.surface: A noisy bug lives next to a field.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny jumping parasite is an insect.

clue.text: Featureless accommodation

definitions.meaning: featureless means level and without interest, as in a dull landscape
an apartment is a place to live

explanation.definitionFit: A flat landscape lacks any features, and in British English an apartment is a flat.

clue.text: Like well-worn sofa OK for retrieving from skip?

parts.note: a tatty sofa needs fresh upholstery, so it is read as re-cover
able means competent or OK

explanation.surface: A shabby couch is fine to rescue from a rubbish skip.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is a British open rubbish container. Read RE-COVER as fitting new fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be retrieved or got back is recoverable.

clue.text: Later on I spy zany celebrity

indicators.note: zany says the letters of the phrase are rearranged in a crazy way

explanation.surface: Someone promises to spot a wacky famous person later.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known figure in the media is called a personality, a celebrity.
